annotations.title: Sorted f16in active waves finish in 68.6k cycles
annotations.note: The four active waves average 68.6k cycles versus 105.7k for token-wave GEMM1. They still spend 56.7% in WAIT and 26.1% in STALL, but each workgroup computes one compacted expert block rather than four independent routed experts. The second resident wave per SIMD is a short rejected/empty candidate and exits after about 0.9k cycles.

annotations.title: f16in also has 2.5k-cycle K-feed waits
annotations.note: At idx 635, the workgroup issues the next B fragments, executes one MFMA pair, and then waits 2,496 cycles at vmcnt(9). Similar wait blocks repeat throughout the unrolled K loop. Main wins through less total routed work and a denser pipeline, not because memory latency disappears.
annotations.suggestion: This remains an optimization opportunity for upstream f16in; deeper prefetching could move the baseline further.

annotations.title: Sorting cuts GEMM1 L2 requests by 21.0%
annotations.note: The sorted path issues 2.707M TCC requests versus 3.427M for token-wave. Its measured hit rate is only 1.8%, but it avoids enough duplicate routed-expert work to reduce total requests and misses. This quantifies the benefit that the no-sort kernel must overcome.

annotations.title: Sorted GEMM1 has a 44.4% LDS conflict ratio
annotations.note: SQ_LDS_BANK_CONFLICT is 310,272 against 1,008,384 LDS index-active events, a 44.4% conflict ratio under WaveScope's metric. The token-wave compact-A layout is much cleaner at 4.95%. This is a baseline weakness, but it is outweighed by sorted work reduction.
annotations.suggestion: An upstream LDS swizzle improvement could make f16in faster still; it does not explain token-wave's current loss.
